topic: Browser-agent indirect prompt injection: user and developer safeguards

primary_sources.title: Google Chrome Help: Ask Gemini in Chrome to complete tasks for you
primary_sources.date: Page publication/update date not established in inspected content; inspected 2026-10-22.
primary_sources.use: Defines prompt injection through web, email, document and multimedia content; warns that auto browse can use open tabs and signed-in sites, make mistakes, and that safeguards do not guarantee protection against all risks. Product-specific to Gemini in Chrome; article does not generalize those exact permissions to other agents.

primary_sources.title: Google Security Blog: Architecting Security for Agentic Capabilities in Chrome
primary_sources.use: Describes indirect injection in malicious sites, iframes and user-generated content, and Google's layered Chrome design. Supports framing prompt injection as an open challenge and examples of mitigations; not evidence of a guarantee or of another vendor's implementation.

primary_sources.title: OWASP: LLM Prompt Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
primary_sources.date: Current page inspected 2026-10-22; explicit publication date not established.
primary_sources.use: Recommends layered controls, treating model output as untrusted at downstream uses, and testing boundaries with harmless data and instrumented tool substitutes. The article paraphrases implementation guidance and does not claim a complete prevention guarantee.

primary_sources.title: Chrome for Developers: Agent security considerations for WebMCP
primary_sources.date: Search result described it as published four months earlier; page inspected 2026-10-22.
primary_sources.use: WebMCP-specific developer material discusses authenticated sessions and controls for untrusted inputs. This source was used as additional context only; WebMCP mechanisms are not represented as features of all browser-agent tools.

primary_sources.title: W3C Community Group: Threat Model for Agentic AI Web Browsers
primary_sources.date: Living Community Group document; inspected 2026-10-22. Not a W3C Recommendation or normative standard.
primary_sources.use: Maps agent inputs, page content, search/agent browsing modes, browser boundaries and action surfaces. Used to support a system-level explanation, without implying formal standards status.

primary_sources.title: BrowseSafe++: Benchmarking Prompt Injection Detection Across Web Contexts, Languages, and Browser Views
primary_sources.use: The paper describes production-observed injection examples, matched control pages and tests across page representations; it distinguishes detection from task behavior. Used only to explain research scope and limits, with no benchmark figures or product-specific success rate in the article. Preprint results are not independent certification of commercial products.

primary_sources.title: Perplexity: Comet Enterprise
primary_sources.date: Current page inspected 2026-10-22; publication date not shown.
primary_sources.use: Search/discovery follow-up only: the page markets prompt-injection protection, domain blocks, browser approvals and task limits for Comet Enterprise. It is vendor marketing, not a technical security specification, and was not used to support a claim that Comet's protections are effective.

public_signals.signal: Search returned Google Chrome Help material specifically warning that web pages, email, documents or multimedia can carry prompt-injection instructions for Gemini in Chrome auto browse.
public_signals.evidence: Raw search result followed by direct inspection of the official help page.
public_signals.interpretation: A first-party product help page makes this a current user-facing safety topic. This is not search-volume, traffic, ranking or demand-frequency evidence.

public_signals.signal: Search returned BrowseSafe++ as a recent arXiv paper; direct inspection confirms submission on 2026-10-12 and scope across browser views, languages and matched page pairs.
public_signals.evidence: Raw search result plus arXiv abstract/full text inspection.
public_signals.interpretation: Timely research context for a practical explainer. It does not establish universal attack rates or the status of any browser product.

public_signals.signal: Search surfaced Google's Chrome security architecture post, Chrome WebMCP agent-security guidance, an OWASP prevention cheat sheet and the W3C Community Group agentic-browser threat model.
public_signals.evidence: Raw search results followed by direct inspection of the identified pages.
public_signals.interpretation: Several first-party and security-community sources now address the same concrete risk. Search result placement is not a measure of audience demand.

intent_and_originality.distinct_intent: Practical user and developer guidance for recognizing and containing indirect prompt injection while an agent reads browser content; centers authenticated tabs, action review and incident response.
intent_and_originality.existing_topic_boundary: Related AI-browser selection, CDP/MCP connection and session-persistence guides cover choosing or connecting agents. This article owns the security workflow and does not duplicate setup instructions or claim that every AI browser shares one permission model.
intent_and_originality.differentiation: Pairs a clearly labeled inert mock page note with concrete scope reduction, action-preview checks, incident steps and a fault-versus-injection distinction. Does not run a live attack or present research benchmark percentages as a product guarantee.
